paragraphs: Mercantile Bank Corporation is a registered bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the "Bank Holding Company Act"). Unless the text clearly suggests otherwise, references to "us," "we," "our," or "the company" include Mercantile Bank Corporation and its wholly owned subsidiaries. As a bank holding company, we are subject to regulation by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "Federal Reserve Board"). We were organized on July 15, 1997, under the laws of the State of Michigan, primarily for the purpose of holding all of the stock of Mercantile Bank, and of such other subsidiaries as we may acquire or establish. Mercantile Bank commenced business on December 15, 1997. During the third quarter of 2013, we filed an election to become a financial holding company, which election became effective April 14, 2014. Mercantile Insurance Center, Inc. ("our insurance company"), a subsidiary of Mercantile Bank, commenced operations during 2002 to offer insurance products. Mercantile Community Partners ("MCP"), our subsidiary, began operations during 2023 to invest in community development tax credit investments. On July 22, 2025, we entered into a merger agreement with Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, the bank holding company for Eastern Michigan Bank. Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation shareholders had the right to receive 0.7116 shares of Mercantile Bank Corporation stock and $32.32 in exchange for each share of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation stock they owned. The merger was completed on December 31, 2025, and Eastern Michigan Bank operates alongside Mercantile Bank Corporation's existing bank, Mercantile Bank (collectively, "our banks"). We plan for our banks to operate alongside each other until the conversion of our core processor is completed in the first quarter of 2027, at which time we plan to consolidate Eastern Michigan Bank into Mercantile Bank. Prior to completing the merger, we were required to obtain approval from the Federal Reserve Board, which we did on December 16, 2025. See Note 17 – Business Combinations for additional information regarding the merger. Our expenses have generally been paid using cash dividends from Mercantile Bank. Our principal source of future operating funds is expected to be dividends from our banks.

Our banks are state banking companies that operate under the laws of the State of Michigan, pursuant to charters issued by the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services. Our banks' deposits are insured to the maximum extent permitted by law by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC"). Our banks, through their combined 54 office locations, provide commercial banking services, primarily to small- to medium-sized businesses, and retail banking services. Mercantile Bank's main office is located in Grand Rapids, Michigan, and its operations are centered around the West and Central portions of Michigan. Mercantile Bank also has banking offices located in the metropolitan Detroit area, Traverse City, Petoskey, and Midland. Eastern Michigan Bank's main office is located in Croswell, Michigan, and its operations are centered around Eastern Michigan. Our banks make secured and unsecured commercial, construction, mortgage and consumer loans, and accept checking, savings and time deposits. Our banks collectively own 16 automated teller machines ("ATM") and 37 video banking machines, which are located at our office locations that participate in the ACCEL/EXCHANGE and PLUS regional network systems, as well as other ATM networks throughout the country. Our banks also enable their customers to conduct certain loan and deposit transactions by personal computer and through mobile applications. Courier service is provided to certain commercial customers, and safe deposit boxes are available at a vast majority of our office locations. Our banks do not have trust powers.

Our insurance company acquired an existing shelf insurance agency effective April 15, 2002. An Agency and Institution Agreement was entered into among our insurance company, Mercantile Bank and Hub International for the purpose of providing programs of mass marketed personal lines of insurance. Insurance product offerings include private passenger automobile, homeowners, personal inland marine, boat owners, recreational vehicle, dwelling fire, umbrella policies, small business and life insurance products, all of which are provided by and written through companies that have appointed Hub International as their agent. To date, we have not provided the insurance products noted above and currently have no plans to do so.

We have five business trusts that are wholly owned subsidiaries of Mercantile Bank Corporation but are not consolidated. Each of the trusts was formed to issue preferred securities that were sold in private sales, as well as to sell common securities to Mercantile Bank Corporation. The proceeds from the preferred and common securities sales were used by the trusts to purchase floating rate notes issued by Mercantile Bank Corporation. The rates of interest, interest payment dates, call features and maturity dates of each floating rate note are identical to its respective preferred securities. The net proceeds from the issuance of the floating rate notes were used for a variety of purposes, including contributions to Mercantile Bank as capital to provide support for asset growth and the funding of stock repurchase programs and certain acquisitions. The only significant assets of our trusts are the floating rate notes, and the only significant liabilities of our trusts are the preferred securities. The floating rate notes are categorized on our Consolidated Balance Sheets as subordinated debentures, and the interest expense is recorded on our Consolidated Statements of Income under interest expense on other borrowings.

Our earnings are affected by domestic economic conditions and the monetary and fiscal policies of the United States Government, its agencies, and the Federal Reserve Board. The Federal Reserve Board's monetary policies have had, and will likely continue to have, an important impact on the operating results of commercial banks through its power to implement national monetary policy in order to, among other things, curb inflation, maintain or encourage employment, and mitigate economic recessions. The policies of the Federal Reserve Board have a major effect upon the levels of bank loans, investments and deposits through its open market operations in United States Government securities, and through its regulation of, among other things, the discount rate on borrowings of member banks. It is not possible to predict the nature and impact of future changes in monetary and fiscal policies.

Bank holding companies and banks, like many other financial institutions, are regulated under a variety of federal and state statutes and the regulations that implement those statutes. These statutes include, among others, the Bank Holding Company Act, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the "Dodd-Frank Act"), the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protection Act ("EGRRCPA"), the Truth in Lending Act, the Truth in Savings Act, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Expedited Funds Availability Act, the Community Reinvestment Act, the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act, the FACT Act, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, the Sarbanes Oxley Act, the Bank Secrecy Act of 1970, as amended by Title III of the Uniting and Strengthening America by Providing Appropriate Tools Required to Intercept and Obstruct Terrorism Act of 2001, electronic funds transfer laws, redlining laws, predatory lending laws, antitrust laws, environmental laws, anti-money laundering laws, privacy laws, state usury statutes, and statutes relating to fiduciaries. Our growth and earnings performance may be impacted by the statutes administered by, and the regulations and policies of, various governmental regulatory authorities. Those regulatory authorities include, but are not limited to, the FDIC, the Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services, the Internal Revenue Service and state taxing authorities. The effect of such statutes, regulations and policies, and any changes thereto, may significantly impact our business, which cannot necessarily be predicted.

As a registered bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act, we are required to file an annual report with the Federal Reserve Board and such additional information as the Federal Reserve Board may require. We are also subject to periodic examinations by the Federal Reserve Board.

The Bank Holding Company Act limits the activities of bank holding companies and their subsidiaries to banking and the management of banks and to certain permitted non-banking activities. The permitted non-banking activities generally include limited activities that the Federal Reserve Board has determined, by order or regulation as of the day prior to enactment of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, to be so closely related to banking as to be a proper incident to banking. These permitted non-banking activities include, among other things: operating a mortgage company (engaged in certain limited functions), finance company, or factoring company; performing certain data processing operations; providing certain investment and financial advice; acting as an insurance agent for certain types of credit-related insurance; leasing property on a full-payout, nonoperating basis; and providing discount securities brokerage services for customers. Neither we nor any of our subsidiaries engage in any of the non-banking activities listed above.

On April 14, 2014, our election to become a financial holding company, as permitted by the Bank Holding Company Act, as amended by Title I of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, was accepted and made effective by the Federal Reserve Board. In order to maintain our status as a financial holding company, we, Mercantile Bank, and Eastern Michigan Bank, must satisfy statutory requirements regarding capitalization, management and compliance with the Community Reinvestment Act. As a financial holding company, we are permitted to engage in a broader range of activities under the Bank Holding Company Act than are permitted for bank holding companies. Those expanded activities include any activity which the Federal Reserve Board (in certain instances in consultation with the Department of the Treasury) determines, by order or by regulation, to be financial in nature or incidental to such financial activity, or to be complementary to a financial activity, and not to pose a substantial risk to the safety and soundness of depository institutions or the financial system generally. Such expanded activities that have been previously approved by the Federal Reserve Board include, among others: insuring, guaranteeing, or indemnifying against loss, harm, damage, illness, disability or death, or issuing annuities, and acting as principal, agent or broker for such purposes; providing financial, investment or economic advisory services, including advising a mutual fund; and underwriting, dealing in, or making a market in securities. While our insurance company is permitted to engage in the insurance agency activities described above by virtue of our financial holding company status, neither we nor any of our subsidiaries currently engage in these expanded activities.

Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank are subject to restrictions imposed by federal and state laws and regulations. Among other things, these restrictions limit the transactions Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank conduct with us, our other subsidiaries or other affiliates, limit our securities borrowing or lending, derivatives, and repurchase transactions with us, our other subsidiaries or other affiliates, limit investments in stock or other securities that we issue, limit the taking of such stock or securities as collateral for loans to any borrower, and limit acquisitions of assets or services from, and sales of certain types of assets to, us, our other subsidiaries or other affiliates. Michigan banking laws place additional restrictions on various aspects of banking, including branching, payment of dividends, and loan interest rates, in addition to capital and surplus requirements. Federal law restricts our ability to borrow from our banks by limiting the aggregate amount we may borrow and by requiring that all loans to us be secured in designated amounts by specified forms of collateral.

With respect to the acquisition of banking organizations, we are generally required to obtain the prior approval of the Federal Reserve Board before we can acquire all or substantially all of the assets of any bank, or acquire ownership or control of any voting shares of any bank or bank holding company, if, after the acquisition, we would own or control more than 5% of the voting shares of the bank or bank holding company. Acquisitions of banking organizations across state lines are subject to additional restrictions imposed by federal and state laws and regulations.

The scope of regulations and supervision of various aspects of our business have expanded as a result of the adoption in July, 2010 of the Dodd-Frank Act, and may continue to expand as the result of implementing regulations being adopted by federal regulators. However, on May 24, 2018, EGRRCPA amended certain provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act to tailor them to the specific circumstances of various categories of financial institutions and transactions. Many of the statutes and regulations under which we and our banks operate may change in the future, which may significantly impact our business.

As a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, Eastern Michigan Bank is subject to comprehensive regulation and supervision by the Federal Reserve Board and, as applicable, state banking authorities. Eastern Michigan Bank's operations are governed by the Federal Reserve Act and related regulations, including capital adequacy, liquidity, affiliate transaction, insider lending, and safety and soundness requirements. It is also subject to applicable federal and state consumer protection laws, the Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering regulations, and, as an FDIC-insured institution, deposit insurance assessments and related requirements. These regulatory requirements may affect Eastern Michigan Bank's business operations, growth strategies, and financial performance.

We face substantial competition in all phases of our operations from a variety of different competitors. We compete for deposits, loans and other financial services with numerous Michigan-based and national and regional banks, savings banks, thrifts, credit unions and other financial institutions as well as with other entities that provide financial services. Some of the financial institutions and financial service organizations with whom we compete are not subject to the same degree of regulation as we are. Many of our primary competitors have been in business for many years, have established customer bases, are larger, have substantially higher lending limits than we do, and offer larger branch networks and other services which we do not. Most of these same entities have greater capital resources than we do, which, among other things, may allow them to price their services at levels more favorable to the customer and to provide larger credit facilities than we do. Under specified circumstances (that have been modified by the Dodd-Frank Act and EGRRCPA), securities firms and insurance companies that elect to become financial holding companies under the Bank Holding Company Act may acquire banks and other financial institutions. Federal and state banking law affects the competitive environment in which we conduct our business. The financial services industry is also likely to become more competitive as further technological advances enable more companies to provide financial services. We also face new competition as a result of expansion into new markets.

paragraphs: The following risk factors could affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. These risk factors should be considered in connection with evaluating the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report because they could cause the actual results and conditions to differ materially from those projected in forward-looking statements. Before you buy our common stock, you should know that investing in our common stock involves risks, including the risks described below. The risks that are highlighted here are not the only ones we face. If the adverse matters referred to in any of the risks actually occur, our business, financial condition or operations could be adversely affected. In that case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

Our earnings and cash flows are largely dependent upon our net interest income. Interest rates are highly sensitive to many factors that are beyond our control, including general economic conditions and policies of various governmental and regulatory agencies and, in particular, the Federal Reserve Board. Generally speaking, increases in the targeted federal funds rate positively impact our net interest income. In contrast, higher interest rates generally have a negative impact on both the housing market, by reducing refinancing activity and new home purchases, and the U.S. economy.

We principally manage interest rate risk by managing the volume and mix of our earning assets and funding liabilities. Changes in monetary policy, including changes in interest rates, could influence not only the interest we receive on loans and investments and the amount of interest we pay on deposits and borrowings, but these changes could also affect: (1) our ability to originate and/or sell loans and obtain deposits; (2) the fair value of our financial assets and liabilities, which could negatively impact shareholders' equity, and our ability to realize gains from the sale of such assets; (3) our ability to obtain and retain deposits in competition with other available investment alternatives; (4) the ability of our borrowers to repay adjustable or variable rate loans; and (5) the average duration of our investment securities portfolio and other interest-earning assets. If the interest rates paid on deposits and borrowings increase at a faster rate than the interest received on loans and other investments, our net interest income, and therefore earnings, could be adversely affected. Earnings could also be adversely affected if the interest rates received on loans and other investments decline more rapidly than the interest rates paid on deposits and other borrowings. In a changing interest rate environment, we may not be able to manage this risk effectively. If we are unable to manage interest rate risk effectively, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially affected.

Our banking operations require liquidity to meet our deposit and debt obligations as they come due. There are many potential factors that could reduce our access to liquidity sources, including higher interest rate environments, tightening fiscal policy, a downturn in the U.S. economy, difficult credit markets or adverse regulatory actions. Our access to deposits may also be affected by the liquidity needs of our depositors. A substantial

majority of our liabilities are demand, savings, interest checking and money market deposits, which are payable on demand or upon several days' notice, while by comparison, a substantial portion of our assets are loans, which cannot be called or sold in the same time frame. We may not be able to replace maturing deposits and advances as necessary in the future, especially if a large number of our depositors sought to withdraw their accounts, regardless of the reason. Our access to deposits may be negatively impacted by, among other factors, periods of low interest rates or higher interest rates which could promote increased competition for deposits, including from new financial technology competitors, or provide customers with alternative investment options. Additionally, negative news about us or the banking industry in general could negatively impact market and/or customer perceptions of our company, which could lead to a loss of depositor confidence and an increase in deposit withdrawals, particularly among those with uninsured deposits. Furthermore, as we and other regional banking organizations experienced in 2023, the failure of other financial institutions may cause deposit outflows as customers spread deposits among several different banks so as to maximize their amount of FDIC insurance, move deposits to banks deemed "too big to fail" or remove deposits from the banking system entirely. As of

December 31, 2025, approximately 54% of our deposits were uninsured, and we rely on these deposits for liquidity. A failure to maintain adequate liquidity could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: Mercantile Bank Corporation 為依 1956 年銀行控股公司法（Bank Holding Company Act）註冊之銀行控股公司，經修正後之條文（"Bank Holding Company Act"）。除非文義明確另有說明，否則文中所稱 "我們"、"我們"、"我們的" 或 "公司" 皆包含 Mercantile Bank Corporation 及其百分之百擁有之子公司。作為銀行控股公司，我們受美國聯邦儲備銀行（Federal Reserve Board）之監管。我們於 1997 年 7 月 15 日根據密歇根州法律設立，主要目的是持有 Mercantile Bank 全部股票，以及我們可能取得或設立之其他子公司。Mercantile Bank 於 1997 年 12 月 15 日開始營業。2013 年第三季，我們提交申請成為金融控股公司，該申請於 2014 年 4 月 14 日生效。Mercantile Insurance Center, Inc.（"我們的保險公司"），為 Mercantile Bank 之子公司，於 2002 年開始營運，提供保險產品。Mercantile Community Partners（"MCP"），我們的子公司，於 2023 年開始營運，投資於社區發展稅收抵免投資。2025 年 7 月 22 日，我們與 Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation 籤訂合併協議，Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation 為 Eastern Michigan Bank 之銀行控股公司。Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation 股東可就其持有的每一股 Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation 股票，換取 0.7116 股 Mercantile Bank Corporation 股票及 32.32 美元。該合併於 2025 年 12 月 31 日完成，Eastern Michigan Bank 並與 Mercantile Bank Corporation 現有銀行 Mercantile Bank 並行營運（合稱 "我們的銀行"）。我們計畫讓我們的銀行並行營運，直至 2027 年第一季完成我們核心處理商之轉換，屆時我們計畫將 Eastern Michigan Bank 合併至 Mercantile Bank。在完成合併前，我們需取得 Federal Reserve Board 之批准，我們於 2025 年 12 月 16 日取得批准。請參見附註 17 – 企業併購，以取得更多關於該合併之資訊。我們的費用通常由 Mercantile Bank 之現金紅利支付。我們未來主要營運資金來源預期為我們的銀行之紅利。

我們的銀行為州立銀行公司，根據密歇根州法律，依密歇根州保險及金融服務部所頒發之執照運作。我們的銀行存款由美國存款保險公司（FDIC）依照法律規定之最高額度投保。我們的銀行透過其合計 54 處分行，提供商業銀行服務，主要服務小型至中型企業，以及零售銀行服務。Mercantile Bank 之總部位於密歇根州格蘭德拉普（Grand Rapids），其業務集中於密歇根州西部及中部地區。Mercantile Bank 亦在底特律都會區、特拉弗瑟城（Traverse City）、佩託斯基（Petoskey）及米德蘭（Midland）設有銀行分行。Eastern Michigan Bank 之總部位於密歇根州克勞斯威爾（Croswell），其業務集中於東密歇根地區。我們的銀行提供擔保及無擔保之商業貸款、建設貸款、住宅貸款及消費貸款，並接受支票存款、儲蓄存款及定期存款。我們的銀行合計擁有 16 臺自動提款機（ATM）及 37 臺視訊銀行機器，這些機器設置於參與 ACCEL/EXCHANGE 及 PLUS 區域網路系統之分行，以及其他全國 ATM 網路。我們的銀行亦允許客戶透過個人電腦及行動應用程式進行部分貸款及存款交易。我們為部分商業客戶提供快遞服務，並在絕大多數分行提供保險箱。我們的銀行不具信託業務權限。

我們的保險公司於 2002 年 4 月 15 日取得現成之保險經紀代理權。我們的保險公司、Mercantile Bank 及 Hub International 籤訂經紀與機構協議，以提供大眾市場個人保險產品之方案。保險產品包括私人乘客汽車、住宅所有者、個人內陸海洋、船主、休閒車、住宅火災、遮蔽責任保險、小型企業及人壽保險產品，所有產品均由已任命 Hub International 為經紀之公司提供與書寫。截至目前為止，我們尚未提供上述保險產品，目前亦無計畫提供。

我們有五個業務信託，為 Mercantile Bank Corporation 之 wholly owned subsidiaries，但未合併。每個信託成立之目的是發行優先證券，並透過私人銷售發行，以及向 Mercantile Bank Corporation 發行普通證券。優先證券及普通證券銷售所得，由信託用以購買由 Mercantile Bank Corporation 發行之浮動利率票據。每張浮動利率票據之利率、利息支付日、叫價條款及到期日，與其對應之優先證券相同。浮動利率票據發行所得淨資金用於多種用途，包括對 Mercantile Bank 之資本貢獻，以支持資產成長，以及股票買回計畫及某些收購之資金。我們信託之唯一重大資產為浮動利率票據，唯一重大負債為優先證券。浮動利率票據在我們合併財務報表中歸類為次級債券，其利息費用在我們合併損益表中記入其他借款之利息費用。

我們的獲利受國內經濟條件及美國政府、其機構及聯邦儲備銀行之貨幣與財政政策影響。聯邦儲備銀行之貨幣政策已對商業銀行之營運結果產生影響，並可能持續產生影響，透過其執行國家貨幣政策之權力，以達成控制通貨膨脹、維持或鼓勵就業，以及緩解經濟衰退等目標。聯邦儲備銀行之政策對銀行貸款、投資及存款之水準有重大影響，透過其在美國政府證券之公開市場操作，以及透過其對成員銀行借款貼現率之規範。無法預測未來貨幣與財政政策之性質及影響。

銀行控股公司及銀行，如同許多其他金融機構，受多種聯邦及州法律及實施這些法律之規則所規範。這些法律包括，但不限於，銀行控股公司法、多德-弗蘭克壁壘改革與消費者保護法案（Dodd-Frank Act）、經濟成長、監管減輕與消費者保護法案（EGRRCPA）、貸款實情法、儲蓄實情法、平等信貸機會法、信用報告法、加速資金可用性法、社區再投資法、住宅貸款程序法、FACT 法、格雷姆-利奇-布利利法、薩班斯-奧克斯利法、1970 年銀行保密法，經 2001 年「反恐與提供適當工具法案」第三條修正，電子資金轉帳法、紅lining 法、掠奪性貸款法、反壟斷法、環境法、反洗錢法、反稅法。這些法律由各政府監管機構執行，並可能影響我們的業務。這些監管機構包括，但不限於，FDIC、密歇根州保險及金融服務部、內政部國稅局及州稅務機構。這些法律、規則及政策，以及任何變更，可能對我們的業務產生重大影響，而此影響無法預測。
根據銀行控股公司法註冊為銀行控股公司，我們需向聯邦儲備銀行提交年度報告，以及聯邦儲備銀行可能要求之其他資訊。我們亦需接受聯邦儲備銀行之定期檢查。

根據銀行控股公司法，銀行控股公司及其子公司之業務活動限於銀行業務及銀行管理，以及某些允許之非銀行業務。允許之非銀行業務通常包括聯邦儲備銀行於格雷姆-利奇-布利利法通過前之命令或規則所認定，與銀行密切相關，且為銀行業務之適當附屬活動。這些允許之非銀行業務包括，但不限於：經營抵押公司（從事某些有限功能）、金融公司或應收帳款公司；執行某些資料處理作業；提供某些投資及財務諮詢；作為某些信貸相關保險之保險經紀；以全額支付、非營運方式出租財產；以及為客戶提供折扣證券經紀服務。我們或我們任何子公司均未從事上述非銀行業務。

於 2014 年 4 月 14 日，本公司依照《銀行控股公司法》（經《格雷姆-李-布萊利法案》第一條修正）之規定，申請成為財務控股公司，該申請已獲聯邦儲備理事會接受並生效。為維持本公司為財務控股公司之資格，本公司、Mercantile Bank 及 Eastern Michigan Bank 必須符合有關資本、管理及遵守《社區再投資法》之法定要求。作為財務控股公司，本公司得根據《銀行控股公司法》從事較銀行控股公司更廣範圍之活動。這些擴展活動包括聯邦儲備理事會（在某些情況下與財政部協商後）透過命令或規則所認定，屬財務性質或與財務活動相關，或與財務活動相輔相成，且不對存款機構或金融體系整體造成重大風險之活動。已獲聯邦儲備理事會批准之擴展活動包括，例如：提供保險、擔保或賠償，或發行年金，以及作為主辦人、代理人或經紀人從事上述活動；提供財務、投資或經濟諮詢服務，包括為共同基金提供建議；以及從事證券之經紀、交易或做市業務。雖然本公司之保險公司得根據本公司財務控股公司之資格從事上述保險經紀活動，但本公司及其任何子公司目前並未從事這些擴展活動。

Mercantile Bank 及 Eastern Michigan Bank 受聯邦及州法律與規則之限制。其中包含限制 Mercantile Bank 及 Eastern Michigan Bank 與本公司、其他子公司或其它關聯機構進行交易，限制本公司、其他子公司或其它關聯機構之證券借貸或融資、衍生性商品及回購交易，限制投資本公司發行之股票或其他證券，限制以本公司發行之股票或證券作為貸款擔保，以及限制從本公司、其他子公司或其它關聯機構購入資產或服務，以及向本公司、其他子公司或其它關聯機構出售特定類型資產。密歇根州銀行法對銀行業務之各項方面設有額外限制，包括分行、發放紅利、貸款利率，以及資本與盈餘要求。聯邦法規限制本公司從銀行借款之能力，透過限制可借款總額，並要求所有貸款必須以指定形式之擔保品作擔保。
關於取得銀行機構之事宜，本公司一般需在取得任何銀行全部或 substantially all 之資產，或取得任何銀行或銀行控股公司之股權或控制權前，取得聯邦儲備理事會之事前批准，若取得後本公司將擁有或控制該銀行或銀行控股公司逾 5% 之投票權股權。跨州取得銀行機構之事宜，尚受聯邦及州法律與規則之額外限制。
由於 2010 年 7 月通過《多德-弗蘭克法案》，各項業務之規範與監督範圍已擴張，未來可能因聯邦監管機構採納實質規範而持續擴張。然而，2018 年 5 月 24 日，EGRRCPA 已修正《多德-弗蘭克法案》之部分條文，使其更符合各類金融機構與交易之特定情況。本公司及銀行所適用之許多法律與規則，未來可能有所變更，這可能對本公司業務產生重大影響。

作為聯邦儲備體系之成員銀行，Eastern Michigan Bank 受聯邦儲備理事會及適用之州銀行主管機關之全面監管與監督。Eastern Michigan Bank 之業務受《聯邦儲備法》及相關規則所規範，包括資本充足、流動性、關聯機構交易、內部人貸款及安全與健全性要求。其亦受適用之聯邦及州消費者保護法、《銀行保密法》及反洗錢規則之約束，並作為 FDIC 保險機構，受存款保險費率及相關要求之約束。這些監管要求可能影響 Eastern Michigan Bank 之業務運作、成長策略及財務表現。

本公司在所有業務階段均面臨來自多種不同競爭對手之重大競爭。本公司與許多位於密歇根州及全國性與區域性銀行、儲蓄銀行、 thrifts、信用合作社及其他金融機構競爭，亦與提供金融服務之其他機構競爭。部分與本公司競爭之金融機構與金融服務組織不受與我們相同程度之監管。許多我們主要競爭對手已營運多年，擁有既定客戶羣，規模較大，貸款額度遠高於我們，並提供較廣泛之分行網路及其他服務，而我們則未提供。這些機構大多擁有較多之資本資源，這可能使他們能以更優惠之價格提供服務，並提供較大之信貸額度。根據特定情況（已由《多德-弗蘭克法案》及 EGRRCPA 修正），選擇成為《銀行控股公司法》下財務控股公司之證券公司與保險公司，可取得銀行及其他金融機構。聯邦及州銀行法影響我們進行業務之競爭環境。隨著進一步之科技進步，金融服務行業亦可能變得更具競爭性。我們亦因進入新市場而面臨新競爭。

paragraphs: 下列風險因素可能影響我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果。這些風險因素應在評估本年度報告中所包含的預測性陳述時加以考慮，因為它們可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所預期的結果有重大差異。在您購買我們普通股之前，您應知悉投資我們普通股涉及風險，包括下列所描述的風險。這裡所強調的風險並非我們所面對的唯一風險。如果任何風險中所提及的不利情況實際發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運造成不利影響。在這種情況下，我們普通股的交易價格可能會下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們的獲利與現金流主要取決於我們的淨利息收入。利率高度敏感於許多超出我們控制範圍的因素，包括總體經濟狀況及各政府與監管機構的政策，特別是聯邦儲備委員會。總體而言，聯邦基金利率目標的提高會對我們的淨利息收入產生正面影響。相反地，利率提高通常會對房地產市場產生負面影響，透過減少房貸重組活動與新屋購入，同時也會對美國經濟產生負面影響。

我們主要透過管理獲利資產與資金負債的規模與組合來管理利率風險。貨幣政策的變化，包括利率的變化，不僅會影響我們從貸款與投資所獲得的利息，以及我們支付存款與借款的利息金額，這些變化也可能影響：(1) 我們發放與/或出售貸款與取得存款的能力；(2) 我們金融資產與負債的公允價值，這可能會對股東權益產生負面影響，以及我們從出售這些資產中獲利的能力；(3) 我們在競爭中取得與保留存款的能力，與其他投資選擇相比；(4) 借款人償還變動利率貸款的能力；(5) 我們投資證券組合與其他獲利資產的平均期限。如果存款與借款所支付的利率增加速度高於貸款與其他投資所獲得的利率，我們的淨利息收入，以及因此產生的獲利，可能會受到不利影響。如果貸款與其他投資所獲得的利率下降速度高於存款與其他借款所支付的利率，獲利也可能受到不利影響。在利率變動的環境中，我們可能無法有效地管理此風險。如果我們無法有效地管理利率風險，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大影響。
本公司之銀行營運需具備流動性以應付存款及債務義務到期時之需求。許多潛在因素可能降低本公司取得流動性來源之能力，包括較高之利率環境、財政政策趨於緊縮、美國經濟出現衰退、信用市場困難或不利之監管措施。本公司之存款來源亦可能受存款人流動性需求之影響。大量

本公司之大部分負債為活期存款、儲蓄存款、利息支票存款及貨幣市場存款，此類存款可隨時或經數日通知後支取，相較之下，本公司之資產則主要為貸款，此類貸款無法在相同時間內被收回或出售。未來本公司可能無法依需要替換到期存款及貸款，尤其在大量存款人意圖提領存款時，無論原因為何，均可能影響本公司之存款取得能力。本公司之存款取得能力可能受多種因素影響，包括低利率時期或高利率時期，高利率可能促進存款競爭，包括來自新金融科技業者的競爭，或提供客戶其他投資選擇。此外，本公司或金融產業之負面新聞可能影響市場及客戶對本公司之看法，進而導致存款人信心喪失及存款提領增加，特別是在未投保存款之客戶中。此外，如本公司及其他地區性銀行機構在2023年所經驗，其他金融機構之失敗可能導致存款流出，因客戶會將存款分散至不同銀行以最大化其FDIC保險金額，將存款轉移到被視為"太重要而不能倒"之銀行，或完全從銀行體系中移除存款。截至
2025年12月31日，本公司約54%之存款為未投保存款，且本公司依賴這些存款以維持流動性。若無法維持足夠流動性，可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
